title: Dangermond Preserve — Inferred Creek Water Surface Elevations (m5-v2, Jarrett steep-creek roughness, with NOAA's operational flows to Oct 2026)
snippet: m5-v1's water heights, plus a third set from NOAA's operational National Water Model flows, hourly from Sep 2025 to Oct 2026 (NOAA moved from model v3.0 to v3.1 on 2026-08-18). Public, query-only.
description:
What this is
Modeled water surface elevation (WSE) and water depth for every short stretch of creek (Creek Segment) in the Jack and Laura Dangermond Preserve, California, derived from modeled flow rates, in meters above the North American Vertical Datum of 1988 (NAVD88). The service holds three Datasets: California Natural Flows, monthly, 1950 to 2024; the NOAA National Water Model v3.0 retrospective, hourly, October 2020 to February 2023; and the NOAA National Water Model operational analysis, hourly, September 2025 to October 2026.

How it was made
Modeled stream flow is shared out to each creek stretch by the land area draining into it. The creek bed is the 1-meter USGS 3DEP lidar at the creek's lowest point, with no smoothing. At one cross-section per stretch, a flow-resistance law fitted to steep mountain streams (Jarrett, 1984) gives the water depth; on steep creeks the water runs slower and deeper than with a fixed Manning roughness. Pools behind steps are filled level. The hydraulics are the same for all three Datasets; only the flow rates differ.

Accuracy and limits
These are estimates, not measurements. The stream flows are modeled and are not corrected with gauge readings. We checked the operational flows against only one stream gauge, USGS 11120600 (Jalama Creek), from September 2025 to October 2026: they averaged about 5 times the gauge's flow (about 7 times in January 2026), and the 2026-01-03 storm peak was about 45% too low. The timing of rises and falls is therefore more reliable than the exact heights. NOAA changed the operational model from v3.0 to v3.1 on 2026-08-18, so flows before and after that date are not strictly comparable. One NHDPlusV2 reach (17594937) has no operational flow, so its Creek Segments have no values in the operational Dataset. The water depth assumes steady flow over a bare-earth lidar terrain that cannot see the underwater channel bed. Use these values for research and visualization.

Service
https://dangermondpreserve-spatial.com/server/rest/services/Hosted/creek_water_visualization_modeled_wse_m5_v2/FeatureServer

Technical details

Dangermond Preserve — Inferred Creek Water Surface Elevations (m5-v2, Jarrett steep-creek roughness, with NOAA's operational flows to Oct 2026). Data-Product Version m5-v2 of m5-flowline-profile-jarrett-depth. Shared publicly (Everyone) as a query-only service. Its file geodatabase and raw hourly CSV items stay private.

How it is made: Modeled water-surface elevation (m NAVD88) and junction water depth per Creek Segment. Discharge per NHDPlusV2 reach (NOAA National Water Model v3.0 retrospective, hourly; NOAA National Water Model operational run, hourly; California Natural Flows, monthly) is scaled to each Creek Segment by the USGS drainage-area ratio method (segment Q = reach Q × drainageAreaRatio from the crosswalk (USGS drainage-area ratio method, ratio capped at 1), as m1). The operational Dataset is NOAA's National Water Model Analysis and Assimilation run, hourly from 2025-09-01 to 2026-10-29 (WY2025 to WY2027 files), not the v3.0 retrospective: NOAA switched the operational model from v3.0 to v3.1 on 2026-08-18, so flows either side of that date are not strictly comparable, and NHDPlusV2 reach 17594937 has no operational flow (its Creek Segments are null in that Dataset). Flowline channel profile (Jarrett steep-creek depth), version 2: m3 v2’s channel, raw lidar bed, anchor cross-section, discharge and pool-filled water surface, with a steep-creek roughness: Jarrett (1984), n = 0.32 S^0.38 R^−0.16, which needs no grain size, blended from Manning’s n 0.04/0.07 over 2–8% slope as in m4. Time-varying values are stored as Held WSE Intervals: a new interval starts when the anchor WSE or either junction depth changes.

Change: parameter change: Adds the operational National Water Model hourly Dataset (Sep 2025 – Oct 2026) next to the two existing Datasets; the hydraulics and the two existing Datasets are unchanged.

WSE Anchor Point: channelRibbon.anchorLonLat (the anchor station's lowest point, WGS 84) of flowline-channel-ribbon v2, the WSE Polygon Generation Method version built on modeled WSE m3-v2, whose channel this version solves on; its anchorBedElevationM must equal the Time Series anchorBedElevationM. A Creek Segment without a ribbon has no anchor point (null). Anchor depth = wse_m − anchor_bed_elevation_m.

Held WSE Interval tables: One row per Creek Segment and stretch of time in which wse_m (m NAVD88) and both junction water depths stay constant; valid_from_utc inclusive, valid_until_utc exclusive, so every hourly or monthly value can be rebuilt exactly. Junction WSE = the junction bed column of the Creek Segments layer + the junction depth.

Raw hourly values: Every hourly value of every Creek Segment is also stored as one zipped CSV item per water year in the same portal folder. Those items are private; read the same values from the Held WSE Interval tables.

Null values: null_values_note is the Stage 3 warning for a Creek Segment whose values are all null (no discharge beyond the Drainage-Area Ratio Transfer distance, or a segment lying wholly on a breached road or railroad fill); null otherwise. Such a segment's wse_m and junction depths stay null in every table.

Channel: Solved on the channel of modeled WSE m3-v2; draw it with that version's channel-ribbon polygons.

Versioning: append-only. Every Data-Product Version has its own service; layer and table names carry the version label. Earlier versions are never overwritten or deleted. Times are UTC.

Published from the creek-water-visualization repository (UCS-285, UCS-298).
